literal: At that time Pillar of State Liu Fang was kept at a distance; Ben urged Fang and Senior Pillar of State Yuan Xie, Li Xun, and Huazhou Inspector Zhang Bin to plot removing Jiong and Wei so the five could jointly assist in government.
idiomatic: Pillar Liu Fang was estranged; Ben urged Fang, senior pillar Yuan Xie, Li Xun, and Huazhou inspector Zhang Bin to oust Jiong and Wei and rule together.

literal: They also plotted deposition and enthronement because the Prince of Jin was the emperor's beloved son.
idiomatic: They also plotted to depose the heir because Prince of Jin was the emperor's favorite.

literal: He again told the Crown Prince privately, "Ben will often visit Your Highness and fears imperial blame; I beg you to discern my humble heart."
idiomatic: He told the crown prince privately, "I shall often visit you and fear blame from above; please see my humble heart."

literal: " When the plot leaked, Fang and the others laid blame on Bin and Ben.
idiomatic: When the plot leaked, Fang and the others blamed Bin and Ben.

literal: The lords memorialized that the two deserved death; the Emperor, because of old ties from before he rose, could not bear to execute them and only struck their names from the rolls.
idiomatic: The lords said both deserved death; the emperor, remembering ties before he rose, spared them and only struck their names.

literal: Bin died before long.
idiomatic: Bin soon died.

literal: After more than a year Ben recovered his noble rank and was made Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies.
idiomatic: After a year Ben recovered rank and was acting grand master of ceremonies.

literal: Because the ancient palace bell-stands numbered seven or eight and additions and reductions differed, and successive Confucians debated without fixed standard, he submitted a memorial saying, "From the Yin dynasty upward the five tones were used in common.
idiomatic: Because palace bell-stands numbered seven or eight with no fixed standard, he memorialized, "From Yin upward five tones were common.

literal: When King Wu of Zhou conquered Yin he obtained the response of the Quail Fire and Heavenly Team—its pitch used seven.
idiomatic: When Zhou King Wu conquered Yin he got the Quail Fire and Heavenly Team response—seven tones.

literal: When Han arose, the responding bell was added, so sixteen bells hung on one stand.
idiomatic: When Han arose the responding bell was added—sixteen bells on one stand.

literal: Zheng Xuan's note on the Rites of Zhou says, 'Two times eight is sixteen for a stand'—this is the meaning of seven or eight; it is of long standing.
idiomatic: Zheng Xuan on the Rites of Zhou says two eights make sixteen on a stand—the seven-or-eight meaning is ancient.

literal: Yet ages have had changes and use and abandonment differ.
idiomatic: Yet ages changed and use differed.

literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou again changed the stand to seven and made the Forest Bell the keynote,
idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou again set seven bells and made Forest Bell keynote,

literal: music is the root of government; therefore to shift custom and change practice nothing is better than music—hence Wu Zha watched and distinguished rise and fall.
idiomatic: music is the root of government; to shift custom nothing beats music—hence Wu Zha watched and judged rise and fall.

literal: Thus music moves Heaven and earth and touches ghosts and spirits; feeling bursts into sound and safety or peril responds.
idiomatic: Music moves heaven and earth and touches spirits; feeling becomes sound and safety or peril responds.

literal: Zhou Wu's taking Forest Bell as keynote was surely a sign of impending ruin.
idiomatic: Zhou Wu's Forest Bell keynote was a sign of ruin.

literal: Moreover the Forest Bell pipe is precisely the meaning of Yellow Bell generating below.
idiomatic: The Forest Bell pipe is Yellow Bell generating below.

literal: Yellow Bell is the ruler, yet generated from the subject—clear in the imperial house's correspondence to the nine-five.
idiomatic: Yellow Bell is ruler yet generated from subject—clear for the house's nine-five.

literal: Yin is the subject yet occupies the ruler's position—further showing the state's omen of ascending the throne.
idiomatic: Yin, the subject, occupies the ruler's place—further showing the throne omen.

literal: This truly matches hidden numbers and is not a matter of human affairs.
idiomatic: This matches hidden numbers, not human affairs.

literal: I have heard that the Five Emperors did not continue one another's music and the Three Kings did not inherit one another's rites—this is surely reforming institutions to the times without losing elegant correctness.
idiomatic: I hear the Five Emperors did not continue one another's music nor the Three Kings one another's rites—reforming to the times without losing correctness.

literal: " The Emperor in the end followed him, changed seven stands to eight, and made Yellow Bell the keynote.
idiomatic: The emperor followed, changed seven stands to eight, and made Yellow Bell keynote.

literal: He ordered Ben together with Equal-in-Honor Yang Qinghe to revise Zhou and Qi pitch-pipes.
idiomatic: He ordered Ben and equal-in-honor Yang Qinghe to revise Zhou and Qi pitch-pipes.

literal: Before long he served in succession as Inspector of Ying, Guo, and Huai.
idiomatic: Soon he was inspector of Ying, Guo, and Huai in turn.

literal: At Huai he diverted the Qin River east—calling it the Benefit-the-People Canal—and sent a branch into Wen County as the Warm-Moist Canal to irrigate salty fields; people relied on the benefit.
idiomatic: At Huai he diverted the Qin east as the Benefit-the-People Canal and into Wen as the Warm-Moist Canal to irrigate salty fields.

literal: Later as Inspector of Qi he sold official grain for himself and was struck from the rolls.
idiomatic: Later as Qi inspector he sold official grain for himself and was struck off.

literal: Later following the emperor to Luoyang, the Emperor said at ease, "When I first was Grand Marshal and then directed all affairs, I kept you constantly at my side—we were truly old friends in grace.
idiomatic: Later at Luoyang the emperor said, "When I was grand marshal and directed all affairs I kept you at my side—we were old friends in grace.

literal: Had you been without fault, your rank would have equaled Gao Jiong's.
idiomatic: Without fault your rank would have equaled Gao Jiong's.

literal: Because you associated with wicked men you were dismissed.
idiomatic: Because you joined wicked men you were dismissed.

literal: Thinking of past grace, I again gave you a shepherd's post—why did you not think to repay and come to this!
idiomatic: Remembering past grace I gave you a province again—why not repay instead of this!

literal: I could not bear to kill you; that was bending the law to show private favor.
idiomatic: I could not kill you—that was bending law for private favor.

literal: " Ben prostrated himself and apologized.
idiomatic: Ben prostrated and apologized.

literal: An edict restored his original office.
idiomatic: An edict restored his office.

literal: Several days later, in audience he missed the mark; he again recounted his merits and had resentful words.
idiomatic: Days later in audience he missed the mark, recounted merits, and spoke with resentment.

literal: The Emperor was greatly angered and told the lords, "I was going to give Ben one province—seeing this, he cannot be used again."
idiomatic: The emperor was furious and told the lords, "I would give Ben one province—seeing this, he cannot be used again."

literal: Later the Crown Prince spoke for him, saying, "These men all had merit in establishing the mandate; though their conduct is frivolous and dangerous, they truly cannot be cast away."
idiomatic: Later the crown prince said, "These men helped establish the mandate; though frivolous, they should not be cast away."

literal: The Emperor said, "I have bent them down and preserved their lives.
idiomatic: The emperor said, "I bent them down and kept them alive.

literal: But for Liu Fang, Zheng Yi, and Ben, Liu Qiu, Huangfu Ji, and the like, I would not be here.
idiomatic: Without Liu Fang, Zheng Yi, Ben, Liu Qiu, Huangfu Ji, and the like I would not be here.

literal: Yet such men are all turncoats.
idiomatic: Yet they are all turncoats.

literal: In Emperor Xuan of Zhou's time they gained favor through rascality.
idiomatic: Under Zhou Emperor Xuan they gained favor through rascality.

literal: When the Emperor was gravely ill, Yan Zhiyi and others asked that the Prince of Zhao assist in government; this crowd acted fraudulently and entrusted the mandate to me.
idiomatic: When the emperor was gravely ill, Yan Zhiyi asked the Prince of Zhao to assist; this crowd cheated and entrusted the mandate to me.

literal: When I was about to govern they wanted to throw it into chaos again—hence Fang's great treason before and Yi's witchcraft after.
idiomatic: When I was about to govern they wanted chaos again—hence Fang's treason before and Yi's witchcraft after.

literal: Men like Ben were all dissatisfied; employ them and they are insubordinate, send them away and they resent—hard to trust; it is not that I cast them away.
idiomatic: Men like Ben were dissatisfied; employed they were insubordinate, sent away they resented—hard to trust; I did not cast them away lightly.

literal: Those who see this sometimes whisper that I was stingy toward merit—men—that is not so.
idiomatic: Some whisper I was stingy toward merit—that is not so.

literal: Su Wei advanced and said, "Emperor Guangwu of Han wished to preserve his merit-holders and all made them marquises attending court; Your Majesty's humane nurture may again use this way to settle them."
idiomatic: Su Wei said, "Han Guangwu wished to preserve merit-holders as marquises attending court; Your Majesty may use that way to settle them."

literal: The Emperor said, "So."
idiomatic: The emperor said, "So."

literal: " He was then dismissed and died at home.
idiomatic: He was dismissed and died at home.

literal: Yong, styled Jili, was a cousin of Jingyu.
idiomatic: Yong, styled Jili, was Jingyu's cousin.

literal: Father Bi was Administrator of Xiapi under Wei.
idiomatic: His father Bi was Wei's Xiapi administrator.

literal: Yong at first studied with Jingyu; their uncle Tong said, "The white-haired one will excel through letters, Jili will reach the martial way.
idiomatic: Yong first studied with Jingyu; uncle Tong said, "The white-haired will excel in letters, Jili in arms.

literal: To raise our house—these two sons."
idiomatic: To raise our house—these two."

literal: The Youzhou rebel Pugu Xing made Yong King of Fanyang for the commandery when he was eighteen.
idiomatic: Youzhou rebel Pugu Xing made Yong King of Fanyang at eighteen.

literal: Later Ge Rong also made Yong King of Yan.
idiomatic: Later Ge Rong also made him King of Yan.

literal: When Qi Emperor Shenwu raised troops, Lu Wenwei summoned him and he did not respond.
idiomatic: When Qi Emperor Shenwu raised troops, Lu Wenwei summoned him and he did not come.

literal: After the Erzhu clan was destroyed he went to Jinyang.
idiomatic: After the Erzhu were destroyed he went to Jinyang.

literal: Shenwu appointed him Chief Clerk in the Chancellor's Office.
idiomatic: Shenwu made him chief clerk in the chancellor's office.

literal: When Shanxi had frost and famine, transport of Shandong rent was ordered—all loads must be full; violators were punished.
idiomatic: When Shanxi had frost famine, Shandong rent was transported—loads must be full or punished.

literal: Yong was ordered to oversee the matter.
idiomatic: Yong was ordered to oversee it.

literal: The commandery princess of Xiangjun falsely hired more than a thousand carts; Yong impeached her.
idiomatic: Xiangjun commandery princess falsely hired 1,000+ carts; Yong impeached her.

literal: The princess complained to Shenwu, yet Yong held to the law without wavering.
idiomatic: She complained to Shenwu, yet Yong held to law.

literal: Shenwu told Guo Xiu, "Lu Yong is stern and has an air no one may offend—truly a public man.
idiomatic: Shenwu told Guo Xiu, "Lu Yong is stern and unoffendable—a true public man.

literal: " He was about to entrust him with great affairs—not only collecting rent.
idiomatic: I shall entrust great affairs—not only rent."

literal: Later he acted for Luozhou.
idiomatic: Later he acted for Luozhou.

literal: At the beginning of Yuanxiang, the imperial army besieged Guangzhou without taking it; Mobile Secretariat Hou Jing, hearing Western Wei relief was coming, gathered the generals to discuss.
idiomatic: At Yuanxiang's opening the army besieged Guangzhou; Hou Jing, hearing Western Wei relief was near, called the generals.

literal: Yong asked to advance and observe the situation; he then led a hundred horsemen, each leading a spare horse.
idiomatic: Yong asked to scout; he led a hundred horsemen, each with a spare horse.

literal: Reaching Mount Daqiu, he learned Western Wei General Li Jinghe was coming.
idiomatic: At Mount Daqiu he learned Li Jinghe was coming.

literal: Yong set many banners on treetops, divided the horsemen into dozens of squads, sounded horns, and charged straight ahead.
idiomatic: Yong set banners in trees, split into dozens of squads, sounded horns, and charged.

literal: He captured Western Wei Equal-in-Honor Cheng Hua, beheaded Equal-in-Honor Wang Zhengman, and returned.
idiomatic: He captured equal-in-honor Cheng Hua, beheaded equal-in-honor Wang Zhengman, and returned.

literal: He was transferred again to Inspector of Yang and garrisoned Yiyang.
idiomatic: He was made Yang inspector and garrisoned Yiyang.

literal: Rebels Han Mulan and Chen Xin were constant border troubles; Yong routed them badly.
idiomatic: Rebels Han Mulan and Chen Xin troubled the border; Yong routed them.

literal: He memorialized asking to enter court; Shenwu sent Yong a letter saying, "I entrusted you with Yangzhou to sleep on high pillows without worry for the southwest.
idiomatic: He asked to enter court; Shenwu wrote, "I entrusted Yangzhou to you to sleep high without southwest worry.

literal: Memorials should stop—among the Han men none should rank before you."
idiomatic: Stop memorials—among Han men none should rank before you."

literal: He died at thirty-two.
idiomatic: He died at thirty-two.

literal: Yong had five hundred horses and privately made armor and weapons; in his final memorial he presented them all.
idiomatic: Yong had 500 horses and private armor; his final memorial presented all.

literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Works and Inspector of Ji with posthumous title Wuzhen.
idiomatic: He was posthumously minister of works and Ji inspector, posthumous title Wuzhen.

literal: Dan was originally named Gongzu.
idiomatic: Dan was originally named Gongzu.

literal: Great-grandfather Yan was erudite, skilled in clerical script, and famed in the world;
idiomatic: Great-grandfather Yan was erudite, skilled in clerical script, famed in the world;

literal: he served the Murong clan as Attendant at the Yellow Gate and Administrator of Yingqiu and Chengzhou.
idiomatic: he served Murong as yellow-gate attendant and Yingqiu and Chengzhou administrator.

literal: Grandfather Shou was Crown Prince's Reader;
idiomatic: Grandfather Shou was crown prince's reader;

literal: when the Murong fell he entered Wei as Administrator of Lu.
idiomatic: when Murong fell he entered Wei as Lu administrator.

literal: Father Shuren at eighteen was summoned as commandery chief clerk, nominated as Outstanding Talent, and made Extra Gentleman;
idiomatic: Father Shuren at eighteen was commandery chief clerk, nominated outstanding talent, made extra gentleman;

literal: because his parents were old he declined and returned to nurture them.
idiomatic: his parents were old so he declined and returned to nurture them.

literal: After both parents died he mourned in devastation six years, personally built the tombs, and had the will to end his days there.
idiomatic: After they died he mourned six years, built tombs himself, and meant to end his days there.

literal: In the Jingming era he was summoned to Luoyang and made Martial Tiger Guard Central Commander—not his liking.
idiomatic: In Jingming he was summoned to Luoyang as martial tiger central commander—not his liking.

literal: Soon he was made Pacifying-the-Distant General and Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, and both times claimed illness and did not attend court.
idiomatic: Soon pacifying-distant general and regular attendant—both times illness kept him from court.

literal: He then went out as Youzhou Marshal and again declined and returned home.
idiomatic: He went out as Youzhou marshal and again returned home.

literal: At the time all praised his lofty conduct.
idiomatic: All praised his lofty conduct.

literal: Dan was a clansman cousin of Dushi.
idiomatic: Dan was cousin to Dushi.

literal: Clever and bright from youth, erudite, with literary color.
idiomatic: Clever from youth, erudite, with literary color.

literal: The commandery summoned him as Merit Officer; the province nominated him as Outstanding Talent—he did not obtain office.
idiomatic: Commandery summoned him as merit officer; province nominated outstanding talent—he did not obtain office.

literal: He began as Attending Censor, rose to Assistant-to-the-State General, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Youzhou Deputy Governor, and Chief Clerk of the Beiyu Commander's Office.
idiomatic: He began as attending censor, rose to assistant-state general, grand master, Youzhou deputy, and Beiyu headquarters chief clerk.

literal: When Inspector Gao Zhongmi surrendered the province to Western Wei and sent Grand General Li Yuan with an army to aid, Dan with civil and military officials—more than two thousand—received the great army.
idiomatic: When Gao Zhongmi surrendered to Western Wei and Li Yuan came with troops, Dan with 2,000+ civil and military men received the army.

literal: For merit he was made Pacifying-the-East General and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, enfeoffed Marquis of Gu'an.
idiomatic: For merit he was pacifying-east general, grand master with golden seal, Marquis of Gu'an.

literal: Soon he was added Regular Attendant and made Attendant at the Yellow Gate.
idiomatic: Soon regular attendant and yellow-gate attendant.

literal: The Wei Emperor edicted, "A classics teacher is easy to find; a human teacher is hard to obtain.
idiomatic: The Wei emperor edicted, "A classics teacher is easy; a human teacher is hard.

literal: My sons are growing; I wish to make you their teacher."
idiomatic: My sons are growing; I wish you to teach them."

literal: He thereupon personally visited the Prince of Jin's residence and ordered the Prince of Jin and below all to bow to him before the Emperor; he was therefore given the name Dan.
idiomatic: He visited the Prince of Jin's residence and ordered the prince and below to bow before the emperor; he was therefore named Dan.

literal: He was added Pacifying-the-East General and Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
idiomatic: Added pacifying-east general and regular attendant.

literal: Zhou Emperor Wen also, because Dan was a Confucian lineage head praised by the age, made him Director of the National University and advanced him to Chariot-and-Horse Grand General and Equal in Honor with the Three Dukes.
idiomatic: Emperor Wen, because Dan was a praised Confucian head, made him national university director and chariot-and-horse grand general, equal in honor.

literal: In the second year of Emperor Gong he was made Director of the Secretariat; later he died of illness.
idiomatic: In Emperor Gong year 2 he was secretariat director; later he died of illness.
